solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Manservant's short speech expressing farewell

indicators.note: short says the manservant's word loses its final letter, cut off at the end

parts.note: a valet is a gentleman's personal manservant
diction is manner of speech or enunciation

explanation.surface: A butler gives a brief address as he says goodbye to the household.
explanation.walkthrough: The manservant's word loses its last letter, as 'short' signals; 'expressing' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A valediction is a formal leave-taking, a speech or statement bidding goodbye.

clue.text: Guest given vermouth in shade

indicators.note: in says the vermouth goes inside the word for shade

parts.note: a visor is a peak shading the eyes
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A guest is handed a vermouth while sitting out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and It is a British cocktail of gin and Italian (sweet) vermouth, hence IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone calling at your home, a guest.

clue.text: Make a late start with invention at home

parts.note: a lie is a fabrication, an invention
in means at home, as in 'is she in?'

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps late, working on some invention without leaving the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a lie-in is to stay in bed late in the morning, starting the day late.

clue.text: Crashed, falling short of the Antipodes

parts.note: a computer system that has crashed is down
under means less than, falling short of a figure

explanation.surface: A plane went down before it could reach Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Down Under is the informal name for Australia and New Zealand, the Antipodes.

clue.text: Money for stamp

explanation.definitionFit: Coins are pieces of money, and to coin is to mint them by stamping metal.

clue.text: Popular female a victim of farmer's wife? That's shocking

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
in the nursery rhyme Three Blind Mice the farmer's wife cuts off their tails, so her victim is a mouse with its tail, the last letter, docked

explanation.surface: A well-liked woman falls prey to a farmer's wife, which is a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' signals that the rhyme's victim has lost its tail: the mouse is written without its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infamous is notorious and scandalous, the kind of thing people find shocking.

clue.text: Low point, coming from Barcelona direction

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bad patch in a footballer's career after leaving the Barcelona management.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, opposite to the zenith.

clue.text: Relative with crushes

parts.note: steps (on) means treads on and squashes, crushes
on can stand for with, as in having something on you

explanation.surface: A family member who crushes everyone underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer 5-2 to read STEPS ON, which with 'with' gives crushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife's or husband's son by an earlier partner is a relation by marriage.

clue.text: Story set to music or a three-part composition about love

indicators.note: about says the composition goes round the letter for love

parts.note: a trio is a piece for three voices or instruments
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A musician weighs setting a tale to music or writing a love trio.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large choral work setting a sacred story to music.

clue.text: Cockeyed with draught — most of kebab is left

indicators.note: most of says only part of the kebab word is kept, its tail dropped

parts.note: a skewer is a kebab, meat on a spit
a whiff is a puff of air, a slight draught

explanation.surface: Something is lopsided in the breeze, with most of a kebab left uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts SKEWER to SKEW; 'with' and 'is left' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Skew-whiff is British slang for askew or crooked, cockeyed.

clue.text: Griped about piano missing in requiem

indicators.note: about here means all around, so the letters are scattered into a new order
missing says the letter for piano is taken out

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone moans that the piano is absent from a requiem performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes P from GRIPED, leaving GRIED, and 'about' shuffles those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song for the dead, like a requiem.

clue.text: Work on engine's air increase

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
up is an increase, as in a price going up

explanation.surface: A mechanic's job on an engine improves the flow of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune-up is an adjustment of an engine for best performance, mechanic's work.

clue.text: Dicky is mature but with energy for a retired professor

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, so the letters are disordered
for says the energy letter takes the place of the a

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An old professor has a weak heart but is still mature and energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps A in MATURE for E, giving METURE; 'Dicky' then rearranges IS plus METURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus is the honorary title kept by a retired professor.

clue.text: Putting last of effluvium in piping is the answer

indicators.note: in says the final letter goes inside the word for piping

parts.note: reedy means high and thin, piping, of a voice

indicators.note: last of says take the final letter of effluvium

explanation.surface: Piping in the last of the waste is the solution to a drainage problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a solution or cure for a problem, its answer.

clue.text: Islanders with little or nothing to look back on?

definitions.text: Islanders with little or nothing to look back on?

parts.words: Islanders with little or nothing to look back on?
parts.note: the Isle of Man breed of cat has little or no tail, so nothing behind it, not nothing in its past

explanation.definitionFit: Manx cats come from the Isle of Man and are tailless or have stumpy tails.

clue.text: Indonesian opossum a tranquilliser's restraining

indicators.note: restraining says the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: An Indonesian marsupial is subdued by a tranquilliser dart.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large Indonesian island, so a Sumatran is Indonesian.

clue.text: 8 failing to start if translated from Latin for even more convincing reasons

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged
failing to start says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: 8 refers to the answer of 8 down, a choral work

explanation.surface: A Latin phrase translated by someone whose musical piece flopped at its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is ORATORIO; 'failing to start' leaves RATORIO, and 'translated' mixes it with IF. 'from Latin' tells you the phrase is Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortiori is a Latin phrase used when a conclusion follows with stronger reason still.

clue.text: Bug one could pick up where I am

indicators.note: pick up means hear, so the word sounds like a phrase heard

parts.note: where I am is over here

explanation.surface: Someone planting a listening device says one could hear everything from here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug a conversation is to eavesdrop on it secretly, catching what is said.

clue.text: Right checking fruit — and very English! — that grows in swamps

indicators.note: checking means stopping or holding back, so the fruit holds the letter for right

parts.note: a mango is a tropical fruit

explanation.surface: A tropical fruit is very English and grows in marshes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangroves are tropical trees growing in tidal swamps and coastal mud.

clue.text: Ideal man using power to protect king and queen

indicators.note: to protect means to shelter inside, so power surrounds the royals

parts.note: might is strength, power
R is short for rex, king
R is short for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A perfect man uses his strength to guard the king and queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Right is the idiom for the perfect partner a woman hopes to marry.

clue.text: Brand's very loud exit

parts.note: a logo is a brand's emblem; the 's is a link
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A brand makes a very noisy departure from the market.
explanation.definitionFit: To log off is to leave a computer system, an exit from it.

clue.text: Lay flat out with no hope of revival

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lies flat out, beyond any hope of resuscitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatally means in a way that causes death, leaving no chance of recovery.

clue.text: Green shoots could be a sign of this core getting recycled? Really?

definitions.text: Green shoots could be a sign of this

indicators.note: getting recycled means made again into something new, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: very and really both mean extremely

explanation.surface: Someone sceptically asks whether green shoots from a recycled apple core signal economic improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: Green shoots is the economists' metaphor for early signs of an upturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic recovery after a slump is what commentators say green shoots indicate.

clue.text: Five broken toes — these should get cast

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: broken says the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Five broken toes ought to be put in plaster casts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' is not a plaster cast; votes are cast in an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballots are cast by electors, so votes are what get cast.

clue.text: At first lost without key in narrow passage

indicators.note: lost means astray or confused, so the letters are disordered
without says the key letter is taken out

parts.note: F is a musical key

explanation.surface: Initially lost without a key in a narrow alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes F from AT FIRST, leaving ATIRST, and 'lost' shuffles it. 'At first' looks like 'initially' but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel of water joining two seas.

clue.text: Story is impromptu one with no depth

indicators.note: with no says the depth letter is taken out

parts.note: an ad lib is an impromptu remark
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tale made up on the spot has no depth.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is an account of where one was, a story offered as an excuse.

clue.text: 1000-1's long odds for Potter's Friend

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in 10K
1 looks like I, the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: odds says take the odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A bookmaker offers long odds on a horse called Potter's Friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is the oven a potter fires work in, the potter's essential companion.

clue.text: Criticised in turn by article in Times

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: in says the article goes inside the times

parts.note: T is short for time, so two times give TT
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone took turns with an article in The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To be got at is to be nagged, picked on or criticised.

clue.text: Leader? Real idiot, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the leader is a true fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a person; it is a newspaper's leading article.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader is a newspaper's editorial column stating the paper's opinion.

clue.text: Swim in calm is happy coincidence

indicators.note: in says the swim goes inside the calm

parts.note: serenity is calmness
a dip is a short swim

explanation.surface: Taking a swim in calm water turns out to be a lucky chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipity is the fortunate discovery of things by chance.
